screening_decisions.reason: This is a methodological paper describing reporting guidelines (PRISMA extension) for systematic reviews and network meta-analyses. It is not an RCT investigating physical exercise in Parkinson's disease patients.

This is a randomized clinical trial evaluating dual-task aquatic exercises in individuals with Parkinson's disease. It compares an experimental group receiving aquatic exercise to a control group. Population (adults with PD), intervention (aquatic exercise), comparison (control group), and design (RCT) all meet inclusion criteria.

This is a randomized controlled trial assessing progressive resistance exercise in PD patients with akinesia and rigidity subtype. It compares an experimental group receiving PRE to a control group. All criteria met: RCT design, adults with PD, physical exercise intervention, control comparison.

This is a randomized cross-over trial investigating a highly challenging group exercise program in PD patients. It compares active balance exercises to usual care. Meets all criteria: RCT design, adults with PD, physical exercise intervention, control comparison.

This is a single-blinded randomized trial examining community exercise program effects on fatigue in PD patients. It compares exercise group to control group. Meets all criteria: RCT design, adults with PD, physical exercise intervention, control comparison.

This is a methodological paper presenting a framework (CINeMA) for assessing confidence in network meta-analysis results. It is not an RCT investigating physical exercise in Parkinson's disease patients.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of Nordic walking in PD, not a primary RCT. While it includes RCTs in its analysis, the study itself is a secondary research article, not meeting the inclusion criteria for primary RCTs.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two types of physical exercise (rebound therapy vs weight-supported exercises) in PD patients. Meets all criteria: RCT design, adults with PD, physical exercise interventions, direct comparison between exercise types.
This is a methodological paper introducing the PRISMA reporting guidelines for systematic reviews and meta-analyses. It is not an RCT investigating physical exercise in Parkinson's disease patients.

This is a randomized controlled trial investigating Baduanjin Qigong (a form of mind-body exercise) in mild to moderate PD patients. It compares Qigong plus walking to walking alone (control). Meets all criteria: RCT design, adults with PD, physical exercise intervention, control comparison.

This is a randomized control trial evaluating Argentine tango in PD patients. It compares tango classes to self-directed exercise control group. Meets all criteria: RCT design, adults with PD, physical exercise intervention (dance/tango), control comparison.

This is a phase 2 multicenter randomized clinical trial (SPARX) comparing high-intensity treadmill exercise, moderate-intensity treadmill exercise, and wait-list control in de novo PD patients. Meets all criteria: RCT design, adults with PD, physical exercise interventions, multiple comparisons including control.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of water-based exercise in PD, not a primary RCT. While it analyzes RCTs, the study itself is secondary research, not meeting the inclusion criteria for primary RCTs.

This is a prospective, parallel-group, single-blind randomized clinical trial evaluating multidisciplinary, aerobic, motor-cognitive intensive rehabilitation treatment (MIRT) in PD patients. It compares MIRT to no rehabilitation control. Meets all criteria: RCT design, adults with PD, physical exercise/rehabilitation intervention, control comparison.

This is a methodological paper describing the development of the EuroQol instrument for measuring health-related quality of life. It is not an RCT investigating physical exercise in Parkinson's disease patients.

This is an epidemiological study and meta-analysis examining male-to-female prevalence/incidence ratios in PD across age groups. It is observational research, not an RCT investigating physical exercise interventions.

This is a pilot randomized controlled trial investigating high-intensity aerobic training with cycle ergometers and balance training in PD patients. It compares intervention to control group. Meets all criteria: RCT design, adults with PD, physical exercise intervention, control comparison.

This is a pilot single-blind randomized controlled trial evaluating treadmill training in mild to moderate PD patients. It compares treadmill training to a control group with regular social interactions/lifestyle program. Meets all criteria: RCT design, adults with PD, physical exercise intervention, control comparison.

This is a systematic review with meta-analysis of dance interventions in PD, not a primary RCT. While it includes RCTs in its analysis, the study itself is secondary research, not meeting the inclusion criteria for primary RCTs.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing task-oriented circuit training combined with aerobic training (TOCT-AT) to aerobic training alone in PD patients. Meets all criteria: RCT design, adults with PD, physical exercise interventions, direct comparison between exercise types.

RCT comparing treadmill gait training vs conventional gait training vs control in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria: population (PD), intervention (physical exercise), comparison (other exercise/control), design (RCT).
Not about Parkinson's disease - focuses on community-living elderly persons. Not an RCT but an instrument validation study. Does not meet population or study design criteria.
RCT comparing two types of physical exercise (tango vs tai chi) in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria despite being a pilot study.
This is a systematic review and network meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. While it includes RCTs, this publication itself is a secondary analysis. Does not meet study design criteria.

Randomized crossover trial comparing cueing training vs no training in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria: population (PD), intervention (cueing-based physiotherapy/exercise), comparison (control), design (RCT).

RCT comparing PMR+visual cueing vs conventional physiotherapy in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria: population (PD), intervention (rehabilitation exercise), comparison (other exercise), design (RCT).
Methodological paper about detecting bias in meta-analyses. Not about Parkinson's disease, not about physical exercise, not an RCT. Does not meet any inclusion criteria.
RCT comparing Nordic walking vs regular walking in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria: population (PD), intervention (physical exercise), comparison (another exercise), design (RCT).
Review article summarizing guidelines and literature on PD diagnosis and treatment. Not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
RCT comparing progressive resistance training vs control in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria: population (PD), intervention (resistance exercise), comparison (control), design (RCT).
Meta-analysis of physiotherapy interventions in PD. While it analyzes RCTs, this publication itself is a secondary analysis, not a primary RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
Prospective cohort study measuring test-retest reliability of outcome measures. Not an RCT, no intervention comparison. Does not meet study design criteria.

RCT comparing balance training with different attentional focus instructions vs control in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria: population (PD), intervention (balance exercise), comparison (control/other), design (RCT).
RCT comparing water-based vs land-based exercise in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria: population (PD), intervention (physical exercise), comparison (another exercise), design (RCT).

RCT comparing Tai Chi + routine exercise vs routine exercise alone in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria: population (PD), intervention (Tai Chi exercise), comparison (routine exercise), design (RCT).
RCT comparing high-intensity cycling vs control in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria: population (PD), intervention (cycling exercise), comparison (control), design (RCT).
Systematic review of Tai Chi studies in PD. While it includes RCTs, this publication is a secondary analysis. Does not meet study design criteria.
RCT comparing power-based resistance training vs control in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria: population (PD), intervention (power training exercise), comparison (control), design (RCT).
RCT comparing yoga meditation vs proprioceptive training in PD patients. Meets all inclusion criteria: population (PD), intervention (yoga exercise), comparison (another exercise), design (RCT).

Cochrane systematic review about exercise for fall prevention in community-dwelling elderly (age 60+). Not specific to Parkinson's disease population. Also not an RCT but a systematic review. Does not meet population or study design criteria.
This is a psychometric study developing and validating a questionnaire (PDQ-8), not an RCT of physical exercise. No exercise intervention is tested.
RCT comparing versatile physiotherapy intervention to control group in adults with PD. Exercise intervention (physiotherapy sessions) compared to control meets selection criteria.
Cross-sectional observational study examining associations between non-motor symptoms and quality of life. Not an RCT and no exercise intervention.
RCT comparing Health Qigong exercise intervention to control (medication only) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
Part Two is an RCT comparing walking training with verbal instructional cues to control group in adults with PD. Walking training constitutes physical exercise intervention.
RCT comparing two types of exercise interventions (treadmill training/kinesiotherapy vs conventional physiotherapy) in adults with PD. Meets criteria for comparing exercise types.
RCT comparing two exercise programs (Agility Boot Camp vs treadmill training) in adults with PD. Meets criteria for comparing different exercise types.
RCT comparing ballroom dancing intervention to control/usual care in adults with PD. Although labeled as feasibility trial, it is an RCT testing exercise intervention.
This is a network meta-analysis synthesizing data from multiple studies, not a primary RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
RCT comparing trunk resistance and stretching exercise program to control in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT comparing power yoga intervention to control group in adults with PD. Yoga is a physical exercise intervention meeting selection criteria.
RCT comparing combined balance and resistance training to balance training alone in adults with PD. Meets criteria for comparing exercise types.
RCT comparing leg muscle power training to low intensity sham exercise control in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT comparing Tai Chi exercise to control (placebo Qi-Gong or non-exercise) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria despite null findings.
RCT comparing Sardinian folk dance intervention to usual care control in adults with PD. Dance is a physical exercise intervention meeting selection criteria.
RCT using delayed-start design comparing early exercise to delayed exercise (effectively exercise vs control during initial period) in adults with PD. Meets selection criteria.
RCT comparing treadmill training (speed and mixed) to control group in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
Consensus methodology paper proposing outcome measures for PD. Not an RCT and no exercise intervention tested.
Review article on epidemiology of PD including prevalence, incidence, and risk factors. Not an RCT and no exercise intervention.
RCT comparing intensive rehabilitation including aerobic exercise to no therapy control in adults with PD. Exercise intervention meets selection criteria.

This is an RCT comparing Nordic walking (physical exercise) to a control group in adults with PD. The study randomly assigned 20 PD patients to NW group or control group, meeting all selection criteria.

This is an RCT comparing exercise targeting balance, leg strength, and freezing of gait to usual-care control in 231 people with PD. Meets all selection criteria for population, intervention, comparison, and study design.

This is a methodological paper about statistical methods for mixed treatment comparisons/meta-analysis. It does not report an RCT of physical exercise for PD patients. Does not meet any inclusion criteria.

This is a randomised pilot study comparing somatosensory focused balance training (immediate start) to delayed start (waitlist control) in 28 people with early PD. Meets selection criteria as an RCT of physical exercise.

This study determines the minimal clinically relevant change for the FOG score using levodopa dosing timing, not a physical exercise intervention. It is a psychometric/validation study, not an exercise RCT.
This is an RCT comparing supervised slackline training to control in 22 PD patients. Slackline training is a form of physical exercise. Meets all selection criteria.

This study compares two different exercise programs (United Parkinson Foundation program vs upper body karate training) in PD patients. While randomization is not explicitly stated, it compares exercise interventions in PD. Conservative decision to include.
This is a methodological paper introducing concepts for network meta-analysis ranking metrics. It does not report an RCT of physical exercise for PD. Does not meet inclusion criteria.

This is an RCT comparing three interventions (strength training, aerobic training, and physiotherapy) in 22 PD patients. All are forms of physical exercise/rehabilitation. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a postal survey study determining minimally important differences for a quality of life questionnaire. It is not an RCT of physical exercise intervention. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
This is a methodological/statistical paper about handling multi-arm studies in network meta-analysis. It is applied to depression data, not PD exercise. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis itself, not a primary RCT. The review objective is to compare effects of different exercise types, so including another review would be inappropriate.

This appears to be a clinical trial of Pilates (a form of physical exercise) for PD patients. No abstract available, but title suggests it tests an exercise intervention. Conservative decision to include pending full-text review.
This is a pilot RCT comparing exergaming to conventional exercise in 20 PD patients. Exergaming is a form of physical exercise. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT comparing water-based exercise to land-based rehabilitation in 40 PD patients. Both are forms of physical exercise. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT comparing an exercise intervention to usual care in 51 people with early/midstage PD. Meets all selection criteria for population, intervention, comparison, and study design.

This study compares dance classes to treatment as usual in PD patients. Dance is a form of physical exercise. While randomization is not explicitly stated, participants were allocated to groups. Conservative decision to include.
This is a pilot RCT with waiting-list control comparing gym training to delayed intervention in 32 adults with mild-moderate PD. Gym training is physical exercise. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT comparing robot-assisted gait training to conventional physiotherapy in 41 PD patients. Both are forms of physical exercise/rehabilitation. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a quasi-randomized trial comparing dance to PD exercise and non-intervention in 46 PD patients. Dance is physical exercise. While quasi-randomized, it is close to RCT design. Conservative decision to include.

RCT comparing HiBalance balance-training program to usual care control in elderly adults with mild to moderate PD. Meets all criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, comparison to control group.

Pilot RCT comparing Hatha yoga intervention to wait-list control group in adults with PD. Meets criteria: RCT design, physical exercise (yoga) intervention, adult PD population, comparison to control group.

Study randomized subjects with stage I-III Parkinsonism to balance and strength training or control group. Meets criteria: randomized design, physical exercise intervention, PD population, comparison to control group.

Study investigates balance training effects in PD patients (PDBT group) compared to PD non-training control group (PDNT). Abstract is truncated but appears to be exercise intervention in PD with control comparison. Included conservatively.
RCT comparing boxing training to traditional group exercise in adults with PD. Meets criteria: RCT design, two types of physical exercise compared, adult PD population.

Study compares RAS gait-training program to two control groups (no training and self-paced training) in PD patients. Appears to be randomized design with physical exercise intervention and control comparisons.
This is a clinico-pathological study examining diagnostic accuracy, not an RCT. No exercise intervention is involved. Does not meet selection criteria.

RCT comparing physical therapy program (balance and gait exercises) to control group in patients with moderate PD. Meets criteria: randomized design, physical exercise intervention, PD population, comparison to control.
This is a cross-sectional analysis determining clinically important differences for UPDRS scores. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention. Does not meet selection criteria.
RCT comparing tai chi to resistance training and stretching in 195 patients with PD. Meets criteria: RCT design, multiple exercise types compared, adult PD population.
RCT comparing lower-limb aerobic training and PD SAFEx to non-exercise control group in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, PD population, comparison to control.
This is an epidemiological incidence study of PSP and MSA, not an RCT. No exercise intervention involved. Does not meet selection criteria.
RCT comparing tango classes to exercise classes in 19 subjects with PD. Meets criteria: randomized design, two types of physical exercise compared, PD population.
RCT comparing resistance training to standard care in 18 persons with PD. Meets criteria: randomized design, physical exercise intervention, PD population, comparison to control.
RCT comparing AV cued task-specific training to conventional exercise and no treatment control in 52 PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, exercise interventions compared, PD population.

RCT comparing exercise programme (strength and balance training) to usual care in 130 people with PD and history of falls. Meets criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, PD population, comparison to control.

RCT comparing high-intensity sensorimotor agility exercise with maintenance to exercise only and no exercise control in PD patients over 2 years. Meets criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, PD population, comparison to control.
RCT comparing agility exergaming to stationary cycling and wait-list control in 74 PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, two exercise types compared, PD population, comparison to control.

RCT comparing physical therapy to no specific intervention control in 40 PD patients with mild cognitive impairment. Meets criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, PD population, comparison to control.

Pilot RCT comparing Halliwick aquatic physiotherapy to traditional aquatic and land-based physiotherapy in 30 PD patients. Meets criteria: randomized design, multiple exercise types compared, PD population.
Randomized crossover trial comparing cognitively challenging agility boot camp exercise program to education control in adults with PD and freezing of gait.
RCT comparing rehabilitation training program focused on mobility, balance and gait exercises to control group in adults with PD.
RCT comparing physiotherapy to general exercise programme in adults with Hoehn Yahr stage II PD.
Feasibility RCT comparing Irish set dancing to routine physiotherapy exercises in adults with mild to moderately severe PD.
Systematic epidemiological analysis of global burden of PD, not an RCT with exercise intervention.
Blind phase II RCT comparing trunk exercises plus falls prevention education to falls prevention education only in adults with PD.
RCT comparing treadmill training with partial body weight support vs auditory stimulus vs control in adults with PD.
RCT comparing body weight-supported treadmill training to conventional physical therapy in adults with PD.
RCT comparing personalized home-based exercise and strategy programme to usual care in repeat fallers with PD.
Pilot RCT comparing functional training, bicycle exercise, and exergaming in elderly adults with PD.
Feasibility RCT comparing best practice physiotherapy to no physiotherapy in adults with PD.
RCT comparing VR-augmented balance training to conventional balance training and untrained control in adults with PD.
Abstract is incomplete but mentions evaluating influence of movement rehabilitation on motor symptoms in PD patients. Conservative inclusion due to uncertainty about study design.
RCT comparing treadmill training to nonintervention control group in adults with PD.
Feasibility RCT comparing cueing exercise and education program to delayed-start control in adults with PD and freezing of gait.
Animal study using 6-OHDA-treated rats, not an RCT with adult humans with PD.
Single-blind RCT comparing water-based to non-water-based physiotherapy exercises in adults with PD.
RCT comparing virtual reality-based Wii Fit exercise to traditional exercise and control in adults with PD.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of exercise interventions, not a primary RCT.
RCT comparing multimodal, functional mobility, and mental/leisure exercise modalities in adults with PD.

This is a systematic review of RCTs, not an RCT itself. The abstract states 'A total of 43 trials were identified' and 'no quantitative meta-analysis could be performed'. It reviews existing trials rather than being a primary RCT comparing exercise interventions.
This is a basic science animal study using in vivo striatal recordings in mice. It does not involve human participants with PD, is not an RCT, and does not test physical exercise interventions.
This is a methodological paper about network meta-analysis techniques (P-scores vs SUCRA). It is not an RCT and does not involve PD patients or exercise interventions.

This is a mixed methods qualitative study exploring participants' perceptions about exercise. While nested within an RCT, this study itself is not an RCT - it uses semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis rather than testing exercise intervention effects.
This is a methodology paper developing a taxonomy for fall-prevention interventions. It is not an RCT, does not involve PD patients specifically, and does not test exercise interventions.

This is an RCT with crossover design comparing physical therapy plus medication therapy vs medication therapy alone in 68 PD patients. It meets all criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (PT), adult PD population, and comparison to control.
This is an RCT comparing a 12-week yoga intervention (n=13) to usual care control (n=13) in PD patients. Yoga is a physical exercise intervention, and the study meets all inclusion criteria.
This is a methodological paper about imputing missing SDs in meta-analyses of antidepressant trials. It is not an RCT, does not involve PD patients, and does not test exercise interventions.

This is a randomized feasibility study comparing the RGRM rhythm and music method (n=12) to control (n=6) in PD patients. While labeled as feasibility, it is an RCT with randomization comparing a physical exercise intervention (rhythm and music method) to control in PD patients.
This is an epidemiological observational study of parkinsonism incidence and mortality over 13 years. It is not an RCT and does not test exercise interventions.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. The abstract discusses community-level action and collective efficacy measurement tools, which does not match the title - this appears to be a review article.

This is an RCT comparing progressive resistance training (PRT) twice weekly for 10 weeks (n=18) to a non-contact control group in PD patients. It meets all criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, and control comparison.

This is an RCT comparing 6-month brisk walking and balance exercise (n=33) to active control with upper limb training (n=31) in 70 PD patients. It meets all criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, and active control comparison.
This is a review article integrating animal and human research on exercise and brain plasticity. It is not an RCT and does not specifically focus on PD patients.

This is an RCT comparing rhythmic auditory stimulation plus intensive muscle strength training (n=43) to rhythmic auditory stimulation alone (n=43) in elderly PD patients. It meets all criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, and comparison to another intervention.

This is an RCT comparing movement rehabilitation strategies to musculoskeletal exercise therapy in hospitalized PD patients. It meets all criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, and comparison to another exercise type.

This is an RCT comparing 12 weeks of twice-weekly aerobic exercise (n=13) to non-exercising control (n=13) in early PD patients. It meets all criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, and control comparison.
This is a general review article/seminal about Parkinson's disease covering epidemiology, genetics, diagnosis, and treatment. It is not an RCT and does not test exercise interventions.

This is an RCT comparing 4-weeks of downhill walking training (n=16) to conventional therapy (n=17) in PD patients. It meets all criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, and comparison to another intervention.

This is an RCT comparing 12 weeks of VR rehabilitation (n=14) to conventional physical therapy (n=14) in PD patients. It meets all criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (VR and PT are both physical exercise modalities), adult PD population, and comparison to another exercise type.
This is a questionnaire development and validation study, not an RCT. There is no physical exercise intervention being tested. The study focuses on psychometric properties of the PDQ-39 measure.
This is a questionnaire development study for assessing freezing of gait, not an RCT. There is no physical exercise intervention being tested.
This is an RCT (40 patients randomized to tai chi or multimodal exercise training) comparing two types of physical exercise in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an instrument development study for elderly individuals, not an RCT. There is no physical exercise intervention, and the population is not specifically PD patients.
This is a longitudinal observational study about socioeconomic burden, not an RCT. There is no physical exercise intervention being tested.
This is a test validation study for frail elderly persons, not an RCT. There is no physical exercise intervention, and the population is not specifically PD patients.
This is an RCT (40 patients with PD randomized to resistance or balance training) comparing two types of physical exercise in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT (34 patients with PD randomized to hydrotherapy or land-based rehabilitation) comparing two types of physical exercise in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT (17 participants with PD randomized to Qigong or sham Qigong) comparing physical exercise interventions in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about risk of bias assessment tools, not an RCT. There is no physical exercise intervention being tested.
This is an RCT (130 patients with PD randomized to aerobic exercise or stretching) comparing physical exercise interventions in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT (62 participants with PD randomized to tango program or control group) comparing physical exercise (tango) to control in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an animal study (mice), not a human RCT. The selection criteria specify adults with PD, not animal models.
This is an observational study about natural history of parkinsonism, not an RCT. There is no physical exercise intervention being tested.
This is an RCT (32 PD patients randomized to Turo training or waiting-list control) comparing physical exercise (Turo/qi dance) to control in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a questionnaire development study, not an RCT. There is no physical exercise intervention being tested.

This is described as a 'controlled clinical study' but does not explicitly state randomization. The intervention is 'behavioral treatment' which is not clearly a physical exercise intervention. Excluded due to uncertainty about RCT status and intervention type.
This is an RCT (40 PD participants randomized to balance training or resistance training) comparing two types of physical exercise in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a cluster-randomized trial comparing healthcare delivery models (ParkinsonNet vs usual care), not comparing specific types of physical exercise. The intervention is about service delivery networks, not exercise types.

This study compares tango dancing to traditional exercise in PD patients (19 PD patients in each group). While randomization is not explicitly stated, it does compare physical exercise types in adults with PD. Included conservatively.
This is an observational cohort study examining mortality risk factors in parkinsonism/PD patients. It is not an RCT and does not involve any physical exercise intervention.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. While it reviews exercise therapies, it does not meet the inclusion criteria for individual RCTs.
This is a randomized clinical trial comparing a high-intensity agility exercise program to a no physical intervention control group in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a randomized clinical trial comparing three exercise interventions (Nintendo Wii alone, conventional exercises alone, and combination) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing a minimally supervised exercise program targeting leg muscle strength, balance, and freezing to a control group in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a software tool/methodology paper describing an R package for visualizing risk-of-bias assessments. It is not a clinical trial and does not involve physical exercise interventions.
This is a crossover randomized controlled trial comparing interactive video-game-based exercise training to no exercise control in older adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a questionnaire development and validation study (PDQ-39). It is not an RCT and does not involve any physical exercise intervention.

This is a randomized pilot study comparing Global Postural Reeducation (GPR) physical therapy to a control group in adults with PD. GPR is a physical therapy/exercise intervention. Meets selection criteria.
This is a randomized controlled trial comparing resistance training to a control group in elderly adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about applying graph-theoretical methods to network meta-analysis. It is not a clinical trial and does not involve physical exercise interventions.
This is a single-blinded randomized controlled trial comparing Tai Chi exercise to no intervention control in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a prospective randomized controlled trial comparing high-intensity exercise, low-intensity exercise, and zero-intensity education groups in adults with early PD. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a parallel group randomized controlled trial evaluating a group-based music intervention in adults with PD. While music therapy may not be traditional physical exercise, it involves movement and rhythmic activity that could have physical benefits. Following conservative screening principles, including when uncertain.

This is a randomized pilot study comparing multidisciplinary intensive rehabilitation treatment (MIRT) which includes physical exercise components to drug-only control in newly diagnosed adults with PD. Meets selection criteria.
This is an epidemiological burden of disease study analyzing neurological disorders across Europe. It is not an RCT and does not involve any physical exercise intervention.

This is a single-blind randomized controlled trial comparing PD-WEBB (Parkinson's disease-weight bearing exercise for better balance) training to a control group in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a randomized prospective repeated measures trial comparing two types of dance interventions (tango and waltz/foxtrot) to no intervention control in adults with PD. Dance is a form of physical exercise. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a randomized controlled crossover trial comparing aerobic training to Qigong (a Chinese medical exercise) in adults with PD. Both are physical exercise interventions. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of physiotherapy interventions in PD, not a primary RCT. While it reviews relevant trials, it does not meet the inclusion criteria for individual RCTs.
RCT comparing two types of physical exercise (Nordic walking vs free walking) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT with three arms: two exercise interventions (balance training with and without rhythmical auditory stimuli) and a control group. Meets selection criteria.
RCT comparing treadmill exercise intervention to control group in PD patients. Meets selection criteria.
This is a systematic review/meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. While it reviews VR exercise trials, it is itself a review article and does not meet the RCT criterion.
RCT comparing dual-task aerobic exercise (water-walking) to control group in PD patients. Meets selection criteria.
RCT with waiting list control testing high-intensity interval training exercise in PD. Meets selection criteria despite being labeled as feasibility trial.

Study compares underwater vs land-based walking training in PD. While randomization is not explicitly stated, the study involves exercise interventions and comparison groups. Conservative decision to include pending full-text review.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. Does not meet the RCT criterion.
RCT comparing three types of physical exercise (high-intensity treadmill, low-intensity treadmill, stretching/resistance) in PD. Perfectly meets selection criteria.
This is a narrative review focusing on pharmacological treatments (levodopa formulations, adenosine antagonists, etc.), not an exercise RCT. Does not meet selection criteria.
RCT comparing dance exercise intervention to usual care control in PD. Meets selection criteria.
Observational/cross-sectional study examining nonmotor symptom comorbidity. No exercise intervention, not an RCT. Does not meet selection criteria.

Title indicates investigation of Qigong exercise effects in PD. Abstract is truncated but mentions 54 moderate PD patients. Conservative decision to include pending full-text verification of RCT design.
RCT comparing two exercise interventions (strength training + falls prevention, movement strategy training + falls prevention) to control in PD. Meets selection criteria.
RCT comparing Ai Chi aquatic exercise to land-based exercise control in PD. Meets selection criteria.
RCT comparing dance/movement therapy to psychoeducation control in PD. Despite small sample size (pilot), it is an RCT with exercise intervention. Meets selection criteria.
Randomized cross-over trial comparing physiotherapy with cueing exercises to no treatment in PD. Cross-over design is a valid RCT design. Meets selection criteria.
RCT comparing two exercise modalities (balance training with vs without rhythmical auditory stimuli) in advanced PD. Meets selection criteria.
This is a narrative review article summarizing long-term effects of exercise interventions. Not a primary RCT. Does not meet selection criteria.

Secondary analysis of data from a large RCT comparing balance training interventions in PD. While not a primary RCT, it provides comparative data from RCT participants. Conservative decision to include for potential NMA contribution.
RCT comparing rehabilitation exercise intervention to routine care control group in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, exercise intervention, PD population, control comparison.
RCT comparing multiple exercise types (Tango, Waltz/Foxtrot, Tai Chi) to No Intervention control in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, exercise interventions, PD population, control comparison.

RCT comparing progressive resistance exercise (PRE) to modified fitness counts (stretching, balance, strengthening) in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, two exercise types compared, PD population.
RCT comparing Wuqinxi exercise to stretching in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, two exercise types compared, PD population.
Neuropathological study examining patterns of neuronal loss in substantia nigra. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention, not a clinical trial.
RCT comparing curved-walking training to control exercise in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, exercise intervention, PD population, control comparison.
Clinimetric assessment of MDS-UPDRS scale. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention, scale validation study.
Cross-sectional study examining cognitive profile in newly diagnosed PD patients. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention, observational design.
RCT comparing tango, treadmill walking, and stretching in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, multiple exercise types compared, PD population.
Review article on epidemiology and risk factors of PD. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention, review article.

RCT comparing adapted resistance training with instability to traditional motor rehabilitation in PD patients with freezing of gait. Meets criteria: RCT design, two exercise types compared, PD population.
RCT comparing aerobic exercise to goal-based exercise and control in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, exercise interventions, PD population, control comparison.
RCT comparing balance training to general physical exercises in PD patients with postural instability. Meets criteria: RCT design, two exercise types compared, PD population.

RCT comparing corrective exercise with balance pad, without balance pad, and control in PD patients at risk of falling. Meets criteria: RCT design, exercise interventions, PD population, control comparison.
RCT comparing aquatic therapy to land-based therapy in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, two exercise types compared, PD population.
RCT comparing Nordic walking to free walking in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, two exercise types compared, PD population.

RCT comparing intensive inpatient rehabilitation (treadmill and stabilometric platform training) to control (pharmacological treatment + generic exercise) in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, exercise intervention, PD population, control comparison.
RCT comparing mindfulness yoga to stretching and resistance training in PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT design, two exercise types compared, PD population.
Review article on deep brain stimulation. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention, review article.
Clinical diagnostic criteria document for PD. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention, diagnostic criteria document.
Randomized controlled trial comparing gait and step perturbation training (physical exercise) to control group in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a psychometric reliability study of a freezing of gait questionnaire, not an RCT comparing physical exercise interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial comparing three exercise interventions (treadmill with music, treadmill alone, home walking) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial comparing three exercise interventions (LSVT BIG, Nordic Walking, home exercises) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial comparing three exercise/physiotherapy interventions (LSVT BIG, intensive physiotherapy, conventional physiotherapy) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial comparing virtual reality rehabilitation to conventional rehabilitation (both physical exercise interventions) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized crossover trial comparing body weight-supported treadmill training to conventional physical therapy (both physical exercise interventions) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

Quasi-randomized trial comparing exercise therapy to control (pharmacological therapy only) in adults with PD. While quasi-randomized rather than fully randomized, it compares physical exercise to control and should be conservatively included for further review.
Randomized controlled pilot trial comparing home-based treadmill training (physical exercise) to usual care (control) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial comparing dance therapy (physical exercise/movement intervention) to support group (control) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial comparing three exercise interventions (flexibility/balance/function, aerobic exercise, home-based exercise) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. The selection criteria specify RCTs only. Does not meet selection criteria.

Randomized controlled trial comparing home exercise program (strength training, movement strategy training) to non-specific life skills training (control) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
